agent-memory-server: Design: one memory bank per install scope (user-scope shared across projects, project-scope local); projects partition via context; shared promotion tier reached ONLY via memory_share (curated, sweep-exempt); workspace_id presence is the isolation declaration (no isolated flag).

Contract artifacts: docs/features/agent-memory/{spec-issue-1.md, agent-memory.feature (29 scenarios), spec.json}. Gherkin .feature is the behavioural contract, gated by .ai-badger/skills/create-task-spec/scripts/spec_holes.py.
Deferred (OQ-8): auto-promotion to shared based on ai-badger stack concept — the IMemoryExtension pipeline (OnConsolidateAsync/OnWriteAsync) is the seam.

Deferred (OQ-5): single cloud memory bank for all agents — V1 syncs committed contexts into one configured SQLite Cloud DB, which is the correlation point between user-scope and project-scope installs.
Deferred: Reqnroll/.feature test runner — spike verified green on xunit.v3 3.2.2 + net10.0 (Reqnroll.xunit.v3 3.3.4) but integration deferred; .feature stays the docs contract.
Licensing: sqlite-vector + sqlite-sync are Elastic 2.0 (free OSS/non-prod); linux-musl-x64 has no sqlite-memory release binary; provisioning refuses with a clear error.

Native extension facts: content-hash dedup is global (cross-context duplicates need preserve_duplicate_paths=1 + distinct paths); defer_embeddings=1 default so writes work pre-model; memory_add_text returns 1 not the hash; memory_embed_pending rejects NULL/0 limit.

Dapper 2.1.79 quirks: parameter binding is case-sensitive against SQL param names; record ctor matching chokes on nullable params (use settable DTO); MatchNamesWithUnderscores alone does not fix ctor matching — alias columns to record names.
Env vars: AIRACCOON_DATA_ROOT, AIRACCOON_INSTALL_SCOPE (user|project), AIRACCOON_SQLITECLOUD_DB_ID/API_KEY, AIRACCOON_VECTORSSPACE_API_KEY, AIRACCOON_TEST_GGUF (gates embedding integration tests).
sync-with-azure-blob: Two sync backends behind ICloudStore, selected by sync.provider row (default s3). R1: exactly one active provider — sync add <provider> deletes the other's rows BEFORE writing (crash between delete and write leaves sync off, visible, never stale secrets; settings merge LWW would otherwise spread them).
R2: unknown sync.provider values route as s3; sync show prints the RAW row so a typo is diagnosable.

Azure ETag trap: the SDK's ETag struct stores verbatim and Blobs writes IfMatch.ToString() (G format) straight into the If-Match header — must construct new ETag($"\"{etag}\"") quoted. Pull/upload response etags come quoted; store unquoted (Trim('"')) to match S3. Pinned by Push_WithETag_SendsQuotedIfMatchHeader.
AzureBlobCloudStore tests use Azure SDK's public HttpClientTransport + Retry.MaxRetries=0 with a canned HttpMessageHandler — no Azurite, no network, hermetic.
sync.objectKey is SHARED across providers (never blanket-deleted); s3-only rows: endpoint/bucket/region/accessKey/secretKey; azure-only: connectionString/container.

Malformed Azure connection string (ArgumentException/FormatException from BlobServiceClient ctor) maps to SyncNotConfiguredException (typed). Pathological container names can still throw ArgumentException at request time — accepted, documented in plan risk 12.
Full-suite embedding/E2E flakes (Embeddings_*, WatchPipelineTests timing) are PRE-EXISTING on origin/main baseline — reproduced without the branch; not caused by sync changes.
